key_insight: Interactive video world models can generate objects passing through physical obstacles, even though their internal representations contain information that could predict these violations. NoPeBench exposes this gap between physical awareness and generated behavior.
problem_solved: The paper investigates how to evaluate and prevent object penetration in interactive video world models, where generated motion should respect solid physical boundaries.
method: Introduce NoPeBench to evaluate how world models respond to physical obstacles.
Evaluate open-source models and find that none reliably avoid object-penetration failures.
Analyze internal representations for information predictive of penetration violations; the provided abstract is truncated before the full prevention approach is described.
impact: For practitioners, the findings show that plausible-looking video does not guarantee physically consistent interactions. They also suggest that existing model representations may offer a starting point for detecting and potentially preventing these failures.
visual_elements: Side-by-side video frames showing an object passing through a wall versus stopping at it.
